topic: Natural Vegetation and Forests of Geography
description: Natural vegetation refers to a plant community that has grown naturally without human interference over a long period. Due to diverse rainfall, temperature, and soil conditions, India hosts a wide variety of forest types.

sections.title: Types of Forests in India
sections.description: Classification of forests in India based on the amount of annual rainfall and geographical conditions.

key_concepts.explanation: Plant species that are purely of Indian origin and are found uniquely within a specific geographical region.
Plant species that have been brought into India from outside regions.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, North-East India
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Receive more than 200 cm of rainfall. Trees remain green year-round as they do not have a fixed time to shed their leaves.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Largest forest area in India - Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Receive 70-200 cm of rainfall. Also known as Monsoon Forests. They shed their leaves for about 6-8 weeks in dry summer.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Semi-arid areas of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Receive less than 70 cm of rainfall. Leaves are modified into thorns or are very small to minimize moisture loss.
Vegetation changes with an increase in altitude due to a decrease in temperature. Alpine vegetation is found at higher altitudes.

Teak is predominantly found in Madhya Pradesh; Sandalwood is famous in Karnataka.
Khejri is the state tree of Rajasthan and is highly adapted to arid conditions.

sections.title: Mangrove Vegetation and Ecology
sections.description: Unique flora found in coastal areas, deltas, and swampy regions adapted to saline conditions.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Negatively geotropic roots that grow upwards above the ground.
scientific_principles.application: Since swampy/saline soil lacks oxygen, these roots help mangrove plants in respiration.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The process where a seed germinates while still attached to the mother plant.
scientific_principles.application: An adaptation of mangroves to prevent seeds from being washed away or destroyed by highly saline tidal waters.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Located in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta, it is the world's largest Mangrove forest and the natural habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger.

important_facts.fact: In India, West Bengal has the highest mangrove cover, followed by Gujarat and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

sections.title: Forest Conservation Policies and ISFR Report
sections.description: Crucial facts from the Government of India's forest policies and the India State of Forest Report (ISFR).

historical_events.significance: Set a target to bring 33% of the country's total geographical area under forest cover to maintain ecological balance.
Enacted to strictly control deforestation and restrict the diversion of forest lands for non-forestry purposes.

important_facts.fact: The India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published biennially (every 2 years) by the Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun.
Area-wise, Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in the country, followed by Arunachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
In terms of percentage of total geographical area, Mizoram (84.53%) has the highest forest cover.
